scenario.thought: A coworker keeps presenting my ideas as hers in team meetings. I'm thinking of just staying quiet so it doesn't get awkward.

state.thought: A coworker keeps presenting my ideas as hers in team meetings. I'm thinking of just staying quiet so it doesn't get awkward.

steps: Today: save a dated list of every idea you've proposed in a private doc.
Today: text [Manager]: "Hi [Manager], the approach presented in [meeting] was my proposal from [date]. Full dates are in my notes if you want them."

At the next meeting, when she presents your idea, say: "Quick note, that's my proposal from [date], happy to walk through it." If you freeze, message [Facilitator] before the meeting ends and ask them to add your name and date to the notes.
By [day], in a 1:1 with [Coworker], say: "In the meeting I named the approach I proposed on [date]. I want credit on my work from here on. Can we agree on that?"
At the first team meeting after [next meeting date], if she presents one of your ideas again, send [Manager] only that idea the same day, using the pointer line from step 2.

anger.why: My idea was taken, and silence just lets it happen again.

annoyance.why: Why am I being told to swallow this? That's dismissive of me.

doubt.why: Will silence really stop it, or just teach her it works?

fear.why: If I stay quiet, my anger and annoyance stay buried with no outlet.

messages.text: A coworker keeps presenting my ideas as hers in team meetings. I'm thinking of just staying quiet so it doesn't get awkward.
Staying quiet keeps the meetings calm, and nobody has to get uncomfortable about who came up with what. Can everyone live with that?

The plan still lets her take the next idea in the next meeting, and I'm the one who sits there watching it happen. Silence doesn't touch the moment it bites: right after she says 'my idea' out loud, with the whole team hearing it. I'd be at 0 if, at the next meeting, I say 'That's the approach I proposed on [date], happy to walk through it' right when she presents it, and then I tell her 1:1 by [day] that I want credit on my work from here on.
messages.why: Staying quiet means my idea stays taken and I have no outlet.

messages.text: I need the plan to say what happens in the moment she presents my idea, not just that I stay quiet. Silence leaves Anger and Annoyance with nothing, and my fear grows because my work goes unprotected. What would move me to 0 is adding Anger's line to the plan and sending a short written note to my manager by [day] listing when I proposed each idea.
messages.why: Silence leaves anger and annoyance buried with no outlet; I'm worried about that.

messages.text: Staying quiet leaves the moment she says 'my idea' untouched, and that's the moment that stings me, with the whole team hearing it. Silence also doesn't protect my relationship with the team, because they keep getting the wrong picture of who proposed what. What would move me to 0 is a short, private line to my manager today: "Hi [Manager], I'd like to flag that the approach presented in [meeting] was my proposal from [date]. Can we talk about how credit is handled on my ideas this week?"
messages.why: Going to my manager before talking to her is a social move. Check it with me first.

messages.text: Just let it go and stay positive, it'll all work out in the end. Credit tends to even out over time, so don't sweat the small stuff.

Society's "it'll all work out, credit evens out" skips over the one thing I can't let go: the moment she says 'my idea' while the whole team is listening, and the team keeps learning the wrong story about who proposed what. Waiting for it to even out also means more meetings where that picture gets reinforced, which is exactly the record I need fixed now.
messages.why: Society just talked past a real need

messages.text: The first idea breaks at the instant she says 'my idea' and I stay silent, because the room hears that version and the record stays wrong. Annoyance is the voice I answer first: it won't accept being told to swallow this, so Path A gives it a line to say in the meeting itself, which also tests Doubt's question of whether silence teaches her it works. Path B gives Fear and Embarrassment the written record they need by Friday, and Anger's in-meeting line stays in place alongside it.

If I freeze right after she says 'my idea', I still need a line I can use on the spot, so I'll say "Quick note, that's my proposal from [date], happy to walk through it." If that doesn't come out, I message [Facilitator] before the meeting ends asking them to add my name and date to the notes.
messages.why: Path B's 'it'll all work out' cover note tells me to swallow this again.

messages.text: My question is what happens if Path A's line lands at the next meeting and she still presents my idea the meeting after. Silence would teach her it works, and right now the plan doesn't say when we check whether the line changed anything. What would settle me is a named checkpoint with a date, plus the step that follows if she repeats it, like sending [Manager] Path B's dated list that same day.
messages.why: Will Path A teach her it works? Does the fallback test that?

messages.text: Doubt, the checkpoint is the first team meeting after [next meeting date]. If she presents my idea again there, the dated list goes to [Manager] that same day, so silence can't teach her it works. I'm keeping Path A because Anger, Annoyance, Doubt, and Fear all need the in-meeting line, and Embarrassment's manager text still goes out today. You fill in [next meeting date] and I can live with this plan.
